decisions.rationale: Verified: section.pep-recap (line 604) and div.pep-cheat (line 610) sit outside every [data-pep-activity]; render() only sets a.hidden on activity sections (line 704) and no CSS keys off data-pep-complete, so both render under Activity 1 from first load. The cheat sheet reproduces the keyed changes one-for-one (label for="email", type="email" required, type="number" min/max, <button>Join</button>, .card { box-sizing: border-box; }, 5 == "5"; // true) and the recap restates them. Workflow 2.3 asks the education critic to judge whether 'any answer is semantically disclosed despite scanner passes', and on a retrieval page this disclosure defeats every activity. Required fix: before an activity settles, no visible recap or cheat-sheet text may state that activity's discriminating answer. Either reveal the recap/cheat sheet only once the page is complete (still printed and present without JavaScript, and still passing T05/T07/T08 print and harness gates), or rewrite both as general patterns that do not map one-to-one onto the Book Swap options.

Verified hint 2 step (line 419): 'Each wrong option keeps one problem. Ask of each: does a placeholder stay the only name, does an ARIA role stand in for a native element, or do min and max sit on a field that ignores them?' names exactly the single defect of A, C and D respectively, leaving B by elimination. Contract, Progressive optional hints: a hint 'does not give the answer'. Required fix: hint 2 must add one reasoning step beyond hint 1 without enumerating the distractors' defects; per-option defects belong in post-check feedback only.

Verified line 539 sits in [data-pep-teaching] above the options: 'A spread copy makes a new outer array, but the objects inside are shared ... == converts types before comparing, while === never does.' These sentences settle distractors A, B and C. They are not among the declared joining details in module.json sourceCoverageNotes (button submits, width: 100% fills the column, async body runs to first await); they are the reviewed content itself, and they contradict the page's own 'Answer from memory first' and the contract rule 'The learner predicts before any teaching.' Required fix: leave only the scenario and the code before the options; any recall of these rules moves into a hint (as a next reasoning step, not a verdict) or into post-check feedback.

Verified: line 537 prints available.join(", "), and distractor A ('Dune, Beloved') depends on join's separator. A search of every artifact.md in html-css-js/{html-and-css,javascript-fundamentals,dom-tooling-and-async,fetch-and-browser-client} finds no join( at all, and the page does not teach it. Contract section 4: 'nothing used before it is taught'. Required fix: either remove join from the traced code (log a form the course taught, with options rewritten to the printed form), or teach join in one short clause before the code; the clause must not touch the shallow-copy/equality traps.

Verified lines 432-435: all four options begin with the identical 'header and main regions; h3 becomes h2', so regions and heading levels named in objective o1 are never discriminated. Workflow 2.3 requires objectives 'observable and aligned to checks'. Required fix: either narrow o1 to what the check actually discriminates (labels, input types, native controls), or make one option vary the structure/heading outline so that part of o1 is assessed, keeping each wrong option to exactly one defect with its own explanation.

Verified lines 498-501: border-box appears only in option C, so a learner who recalls the fix selects C without computing the width; the arithmetic half of objective o2 ('Calculate a card's rendered width') is not independently assessed. Required fix: make the width and the fix each matter, e.g. a correct fix paired with a wrong width as a distractor (or a separate width prediction), so the keyed option cannot be found from either half alone. Each option keeps its own explanation.

Verified: option B is 374 px (= 358 + 16, padding on one side, no border), but its explanation (line 499) addresses a forgotten border ('The border counts too ... Without the border it would still be 390 px'), which is the 390 px misconception. Contract: 'Every option is explained, right or wrong'; the explanation must address the error the option embodies. Required fix: B's width and B's explanation must describe the same misconception (either explain one-sided padding for 374, or change the width to the misconception the text explains), and the arithmetic in the explanation must stay correct.

Verified line 398 (data-pep-fit-good): 'Page regions, heading outlines, labels, input rules and buttons that native elements already provide: they give names, keyboard support ...' lists the keyed change set and favours a real label (rules out A) and a native button (rules out C). Contract: the fit section 'contains no activity answer.' Also verified line 393: 'A div with a click handler never submits anything, so those checks never run' pre-decides option C (a div with role/tabindex). The joining detail declared in module.json is only that a form button submits and so triggers validation. Required fix: rewrite the good-fit at the level of the browser-versus-server decision without the fix list; keep the declared joining detail (button submits, submission runs the checks) but remove or move the sentence that directly disqualifies a div-based control to hint or feedback.

Accepted with narrowed scope. Verified Activity 3's core (const backup = [...shelf]; backup[0].copies = 5; backup.push(...); then shelf.length) is the destructuring-and-spread page's own trace (artifact.md lines 47-49: const b = [...a]; ... b.push({ n: 3 })) with names changed; module.json requires review pages to 'retrieve and apply every module in new scenarios', and a renamed copy tests recognition. Activities 1 and 2 already combine topics (forms + accessibility + semantics; box model + grid column + mobile-first query), and reusing a known misconception as a distractor is legitimate, so they need no change under this finding beyond the other accepted findings. Required fix: change Activity 3's copy-and-mutate structure so it is not the spread page's trace and requires the learner to combine at least two taught topics in a way no single topic page showed; only taught concepts may be used.

Verified: artifact.md puts every hint and the sources under '## Cheat sheet', prints hint-2 summaries as 'Another hint Another hint, 2 of 2 for Activity N', drops hint-1 summaries and omits fit/task/success blocks and the Sources heading. The cause is the shared generator authoring/tools/qa/md-from-html.mjs (line 39 maps selector '[data-pep-cheat-sheet], [data-section-skip]' to 'Cheat sheet', so data-section-skip hints and the sources box are swept in). The contract says artifact.md is 'derived deterministically from artifact.html', so the page author cannot hand-fix it, and changing the generator is a repository-tooling change outside this module branch's scope (authoring/AGENTS.md Delivery). Owner: repository tooling owner, on a separate tooling branch; after that fix lands, this branch only regenerates artifact.md. Not a blocker for this page's correction loop.

Verified: option D's explanation (line 501) says after switching to max-width: 768px 'the base style already gives one column on a phone, and the card would still be 396 px wide inside it'. (max-width: 768px) matches a 390 px viewport, so repeat(3, 1fr) applies on the phone: tracks become (358 - 2*16)/3 = 108.67 px and each card 108.67 + 38 = 146.67 px, matching the SME's Chromium measurement. The verdict is right but the reason and stated width are false, and the real consequence (the layout flips: three columns on phones, one on wide screens) is hidden. Required fix: rewrite D's explanation (HTML and its data-static-alt) to state truthfully that the max-width query applies on the phone and inverts the layout, and that the card still overflows its column; no false width.

Verified line 619: '@media (min-width: 768px) { /* wider screens only */ }' places the rule's closing brace inside the comment-token span, so it renders in comment colour. Required fix: close the tok-com span before the closing brace.

Verified in the recheck bytes (29287ebc...): task step 1 said "Read the markup and the note under it." while the note had moved into hint 1, so the step pointed at missing content and the module.json joining detail (a form button submits and so triggers validation) was taught only in an optional hint. Required: step 1 must match what is on the page, and the joining detail must be taught on the required path before use, without the div-disqualifying sentence removed under edu-p1-08. Checked fix bytes fb12d0c2...: line 397, inside [data-pep-teaching] directly under the markup, reads "Note: inside a form, a <button> submits the form when pressed, and submission is when the browser runs its checks." It does not disqualify the div option, step 1 ("Read the markup and the note under it.") is now accurate, and the sentence no longer appears in hint 1.

Verified: the rewritten Activity 3 uses an arrow function that returns an object literal, (book) => ({ ...book }), which is taught in javascript-fundamentals/functions-as-values-arrow-functions-and-callbacks. module.json sourceCoverageNotes says every concept used is listed in topic.json prerequisites, and this one was missing. Required: list that topic as a prerequisite. Checked: authoring/catalog/html-css-js/html-css-js-course-review/html-css-js-review-page-and-language/topic.json prerequisites now include html-css-js/javascript-fundamentals/functions-as-values-arrow-functions-and-callbacks. fixedInSha256 records the page bytes reviewed alongside this catalog fix.
